title: Helm 4: plain-HTTP OCI registries must be registered with `--insecure-oci-force-http`

detection.reason: a repository Secret's `url` is a VALUE (not collected) and the `insecureOCIForceHttp` key is what must be ADDED — its absence is not a projected fact; the hint names the repository and credential Secrets in the argocd namespace

quote: In Helm v4, the OCI implementation is more strict: if the registry doesn't speak TLS, it is required to explicitly use `--plain-http` upon `helm push`, `helm registry login` and upon `helm dependency build`.
remediation: For every OCI repository (and every OCI chart dependency registry) that speaks plain HTTP, re-add it with `argocd repo add ... --insecure-oci-force-http --upsert` or set `insecureOCIForceHttp: "true"` on its Secret before upgrading. Do not combine it with `--insecure-skip-server-verification` on the same chain — Helm 4 then drops `--plain-http`.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get secret -l argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type=repository -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.data.url // "" | @base64d) | startswith("http://")) | select(.data.insecureOCIForceHttp == null) | .metadata.name' # names printed are plain-HTTP repositories without the flag; add insecureOCIForceHttp: "true"

title: `spec.source.helm.version` is ignored — Helm 4 renders every chart

detection.reason: helmVersion is projected on every Application — spec.source.helm.version (or the first such value under spec.sources) when set, "" otherwise — so an Application without the setting is a clean row, not a projection gap

quote: If you historically have the following setting on your Helm application, the setting is ignored and Argo CD will use Helm v4 only to render your charts:
remediation: Nothing to change — the field can stay — but expect these Applications to render with Helm 4 from now on; re-render them once to catch Helm 4 behaviour differences.
verifyCommand: kubectl get applications -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.source.helm.version != null or ([.spec.sources[]?.helm.version] | any(. != null))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # Applications printed pin a Helm version that 3.5 ignores

title: UI extensions built for React 16 fail to load until rebuilt for React 19

detection.reason: UI extensions are installed into the argocd-server pod by init containers or a custom image; ordinary init containers are not projected

quote: The Argo CD UI was upgraded from React 16 to React 19 in 3.5. UI extensions built against an older Argo CD UI may fail to load with a `TypeError` until they are rebuilt to externalize `react/jsx-runtime`.
remediation: Rebuild each installed UI extension to externalize `react/jsx-runtime` (the React 19 upgrade guide) before or right after upgrading; no action without extensions.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get deploy argocd-server -o json | jq -r '.spec.template.spec.initContainers[]?.name' # init containers printed are extension installers whose bundles need a React 19 rebuild

title: Impersonation now covers UI/API operations, not only syncs — destination service accounts need more verbs

detection.reason: presence-only projection of spec.destinationServiceAccounts on the AppProject; whether impersonation is enabled in argocd-cm is a ConfigMap VALUE and is not scanned

quote: When impersonation is enabled, it now applies to all API server operations, not just sync operations.
remediation: Grant the service accounts listed under `destinationServiceAccounts` on the AppProjects named here the verbs the note tabulates (get/patch/delete on resources, list on events, get on pods/log, create for actions) before upgrading, or those UI/API actions start failing.
verifyCommand: kubectl get appprojects -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.destinationServiceAccounts != null) | .metadata.name + ": " + ([.spec.destinationServiceAccounts[].defaultServiceAccount] | join(","))' # projects printed impersonate these service accounts for every operation from 3.5

title: SSH repositories without credentials now validate host keys against `argocd-ssh-known-hosts-cm`

detection.reason: whether the repo-server image bakes in a custom ~/.ssh/known_hosts is not collected; the hint names the repo-server when it mounts a volume that looks like an SSH or known_hosts override

quote: If your repo server image / pod previously relied on a custom `~/.ssh/known_hosts` (e.g. baked into a custom image or mounted in via a volume) for SSH repositories without configured credentials, add those host keys to `argocd-ssh-known-hosts-cm` instead.
remediation: Copy any host keys you kept in a custom known_hosts (image or volume) into argocd-ssh-known-hosts-cm before upgrading, or credential-less SSH repositories fail with `knownhosts: key mismatch`.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get deploy argocd-repo-server -o json | jq -r '.spec.template.spec.volumes[] | select(.name | test("(?i)ssh|known")) | .name' # volumes printed may carry a custom known_hosts that 3.5 stops reading

title: AppProject `signatureKeys` (GnuPG verification) is deprecated in favour of `sourceIntegrity`

detection.reason: presence-only projection of spec.signatureKeys on the AppProject — key IDs are never collected

quote: Declaring `.spec.signatureKeys` in `AppProject` is deprecated. Configure `sourceIntegrity` in `AppProject` YAML instead.
remediation: Migrate each AppProject named here from `spec.signatureKeys` to a `sourceIntegrity` block (the Source Integrity upgrade guide); the legacy form still works with a warning but must not coexist with the new one.
verifyCommand: kubectl get appprojects -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.signatureKeys // [] | length) != 0) | .metadata.name + (if .spec.sourceIntegrity != null then " (ALSO sourceIntegrity — unsupported together)" else "" end)' # projects printed still use GnuPG signatureKeys

title: GnuPG keys are loaded into argocd-gpg-keys-cm — verification moves to Source Integrity

detection.reason: fires when argocd-gpg-keys-cm carries any key (key names only — the public keys themselves are never collected)

quote: The GnuPG key verification feature has been replaced by Source Integrity, a more versatile subsystem for verifying the integrity of application sources.
remediation: Plan the move of the keys in argocd-gpg-keys-cm to Source Integrity; the legacy configuration keeps working temporarily with a warning.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-gpg-keys-cm -o json | jq -r '.data | keys[]' # key IDs printed are the GnuPG keys still configured

title: `--repo-server-strict-tls` is deprecated in favour of `--repo-server-ca-cert-path`

detection.reason: checked in the Argo CD workloads' container args only — the same setting made through argocd-cmd-params-cm or an environment variable is not scanned

quote: The `--repo-server-strict-tls` boolean flag is deprecated across all components:
remediation: Replace the flag on server, application-controller, applicationset-controller and notifications-controller with `--repo-server-ca-cert-path` (or its environment variable) before 3.6 may remove it; both work together in 3.5.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get deploy,sts -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].args[]?] | any(test("repo-server-strict-tls"))) | .kind + " " + .metadata.name' # workloads printed still pass the deprecated flag
